boards.title: Your First Weekend at University of Oregon, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A low-pressure, under-21-safe first-weekend sequence through campus landmarks, study spaces, museums, and a nearby riverfront route.

cards.title: Start by getting your bearings
cards.subtitle: Self-guided campus orientation
cards.notes: Open the university’s self-guided tour and take an unhurried first lap. Use it to connect names on the map with the buildings and paths you will use.
cards.short_summary: A flexible first look at campus on your own schedule.
cards.evidence_claim: UO Admissions says visitors may explore campus using its self-guided app.
cards.access_notes: Follow the current self-guided tour instructions; route and building access can vary.

cards.title: Find the university’s first building
cards.subtitle: 1201 Old Campus Lane
cards.notes: Pause outside University Hall during your loop, then notice how the older campus buildings frame the nearby quad. Keep this as a daylight landmark stop.
cards.short_summary: A historic anchor for learning the oldest part of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: University Hall, formerly Deady Hall, was built in 1876 and was UO’s first building.
cards.source_title: University Hall | Architecture of the University of Oregon
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is appropriate; respect posted building-access rules.

cards.title: Take the quiet route through Old Campus Quad
cards.subtitle: Historic open space by University Hall
cards.notes: Walk the paths through Old Campus Quadrangle and use the surrounding historic buildings as orientation points. It is a useful reset between more structured weekend plans.
cards.evidence_claim: UO describes Old Campus Quadrangle as the first open space on campus and a quiet, park-like pedestrian area.
cards.access_notes: Use pedestrian paths and observe any temporary construction or access notices.

cards.title: Choose a reading-room reset
cards.subtitle: 1501 Kincaid Street
cards.notes: Stop at Knight Library to locate study options, research help, and the main library entrance. Save a favorite seat or floor for a later study session.
cards.short_summary: A practical study-space introduction at UO’s largest library.
cards.evidence_claim: Knight Library is UO’s largest library and offers individual and collaborative spaces, collections, and research services.
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current hours and any entry or room-reservation requirements before going.

cards.title: Walk the crisscross paths on Memorial Quad
cards.subtitle: Between Knight Library, 13th Avenue, Condon Hall, and Chapman Hall
cards.notes: Cross Memorial Quadrangle at a relaxed pace and look for its distinctive walk pattern. It conveniently links the library, museum, and central academic buildings.
cards.short_summary: A central historic lawn and path network.
cards.evidence_claim: Memorial Quadrangle is a UO historic landscape located between Knight Library, 13th Avenue, Condon Hall, Chapman Hall, and the museum.
cards.source_title: Memorial Quadrangle | Architecture of the University of Oregon
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor pedestrian space; use marked walks and observe event setups.

cards.title: Make an afternoon museum stop
cards.subtitle: University of Oregon campus art museum
cards.notes: Plan this stop during current gallery hours and give yourself time for one or two galleries. Bring your student ID to use the listed college-student admission option.
cards.short_summary: A campus art visit with free admission for college students.
cards.evidence_claim: The Jordan Schnitzer Museum of Art lists free admission for University of Oregon and all college students.
cards.source_title: Hours & Admission | Jordan Schnitzer Museum of Art
cards.access_notes: Current museum hours list Wednesday–Sunday service; confirm hours and bring student identification.

cards.title: Use the EMU as your campus hub
cards.subtitle: 1395 University Street
cards.notes: Make the EMU your regroup point for the weekend. Check Guest Services, scan posted events, and use the building as a reference point before heading elsewhere.
cards.short_summary: A central student-union stop for services and orientation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Erb Memorial Union is located at 1395 University Street and publishes its building hours.
cards.access_notes: Consult the EMU’s current building-hours page; hours and holiday closures change by term.

cards.title: Drop into an intercultural campus space
cards.subtitle: EMU mezzanine, Room 102
cards.notes: Visit the Mills International Center during open hours to learn about its programs and space. It is a low-stakes place to see a campus resource beyond classes.
cards.short_summary: An EMU community space for intercultural learning.
cards.evidence_claim: Mills International Center welcomes UO students, staff, faculty, and community members and supports cross-cultural learning.
cards.source_title: Mills International Center | Erb Memorial Union
cards.access_notes: Located on the EMU mezzanine in Room 102; verify current term hours before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Museum of Natural and Cultural History
cards.title: Spend a museum hour with Oregon stories
cards.subtitle: 15th Avenue between Knight Law Center and Global Scholars Hall
cards.notes: Bring your UO ID for the museum’s listed free student admission, then choose a focused exhibit visit. Thursday’s later closing can make this an easy evening plan.
cards.short_summary: A campus museum visit centered on Oregon natural and cultural history.
cards.evidence_claim: The Museum of Natural and Cultural History lists free admission for UO students and is open Wednesday–Sunday, with Thursday hours until 8 p.m.
cards.source_title: Visit the Museum | Museum of Natural and Cultural History
cards.access_notes: Bring UO identification for free admission; check the museum’s current hours and closure notices.

cards.title: End with track-and-field context
cards.subtitle: Hayward Field museum
cards.notes: Visit Hayward Hall during its public hours for a focused look at UO track and field history. Treat it as a final landmark stop rather than assuming stadium-tour access.
cards.short_summary: A public museum stop inside the Hayward Field setting.
cards.evidence_claim: UO Campus Visits states that Hayward Field’s museum, Hayward Hall, is open to the public Tuesday–Friday from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.
cards.source_title: Frequently Asked Questions about Visiting UO | Campus Visits
cards.access_notes: Current public hours are Tuesday–Friday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m.; regular athletic-facility tours are not included on the campus tour route.
